subject: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements

Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — useful conversation. Quick recap from our side so we're aligned on the problem and success criteria.

Pain points:
- Current vendor-hosted model introduces spikes: p95 latency for short (<=128 token) responses ~600-800ms during peaks.
- Streaming UX is poor: first token often delayed, users see long spinner before partial responses.
- Concurrency bursts: peak ~1,200 concurrent streaming sessions during batch processing windows; sustained ~350-450 qps otherwise.

Current stack:
- Frontend web sockets -> backend microservice pool -> third-party LLM provider. No prefix caching. Mostly 256 token responses for chat flows.

Success criteria (what success looks like):
- p95 generation latency <= 250ms for responses up to 256 tokens (ideally 200ms).
- First-byte streaming latency <150ms.
- Support 1,000+ concurrent streaming sessions without >10% tail error rate.

What we'd like from Redwood:
- Feasibility for a short PoC to validate p95 and streaming UX.
- Rough cost/back-of-envelope capacity guidance for 1k concurrent streaming sessions.
- Any security/contract checklist items (SOC2, data residency) up-front.

Attaching a short latency trace and the internal report for reference.

Attachments:
- finly_latency_report.pdf (latency traces)

Thanks,

Sofia Martinez
Head of Product
Finly
sofia@finly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements

Sofia,

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps.

Confirmed pain points & targets:
- p95 target: aiming for 200ms (we'll size for <=250ms as an acceptance threshold).
- Streaming: first-byte latency target 100-150ms; we will validate end-to-end (client -> first token) during PoC.
- Concurrency: design for 1,200 peak concurrent streaming sessions; we'll size warm pools and autoscaling accordingly.

Our proposed approach (initial PoC):
1) Tech deep-dive (30-60m) with Aditya & Dev to map sample traffic, token distributions, and authentication/KMS requirements.
2) Short PoC (2 weeks) on dedicated capacity with streaming enabled and prefix KV caching. We'll run your representative traces and provide p95 reports.
3) Acceptance: p95 <=250ms, first-byte <150ms for representative traces; follow-on sizing & contract.

Please see attached mutual action plan (MAP) with dates and owners. Two immediate asks to keep momentum:
- Can you share anonymized sample traces (5-10 minutes) and typical token lengths by route?
- Do you need an NDA before we get sample data? If yes, we'll sign — otherwise we can proceed under standard MSA terms.

Attachments:
- MAP-Finly-Initial.pdf (mutual action plan)

I'll follow up with Aditya and Dev to book the technical session for next week.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia@finly.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements

Sofia/Marissa,

Couple technical clarifications from our side before the deep-dive:
- Model footprint: do you have a preferred family (open models you've tested) and average prompt+response token length? For sizing I'd assume 256 tokens response + 64 token prompt unless you tell us otherwise.
- Streaming pattern: are you doing interleaved user prompts (many short sessions) or long sessions with many tokens per session? That changes batching semantics.
- TLS/KMS: Dev — can you confirm what Finly needs for KM integration? We can support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private mode or RBAC + audit logs in Hosted.

Preliminary capacity note: based on the numbers discussed, a dedicated pool (8-12x A100/H100-equivalent GPUs with optimized batching and prefix caching) should meet 1k concurrent streaming sessions with p95 ~200ms for short responses. We'll refine after seeing traces.

Could you attach ~5 minutes of production traces (anonymized), and a sample of peak session concurrency times? That will let us run a realistic simulation.

Attachment:
- p95_capacity_estimate.xlsx

I'll coordinate calendar invites for the technical deep-dive. Thanks — looking forward to it.

-Aditya

Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
